correctness.rationale: At λ=±t, projecting the dimer equation onto its λ eigenspace gives T*h orthogonal to this eigenspace. The orthogonal part of z is T*h/(2λ); TT*=4t²I then makes the hub inner-product equation λ||h||²=2λ||h||², forcing h=0. Equivalently the projected equation relates adjacent hubs by a nonzero phase, so one zero vertex propagates to all hubs for a finitely supported state. Each occupied edge then contributes exactly its two dimer sites, and the residual condition is precisely the signed magnetic incidence equation. Its nonzero support has no degree-one vertex. A graph with minimum degree two and at most six edges is a single cycle: two distinct square cycles can share at most one edge, and a distinct cycle cannot be contained in a simple six-cycle. No even cycles shorter than four exist, and four- and six-cycles enclose one and two squares respectively. They are admissible exactly at the stated holonomies. In the seven-edge witness at the displayed origin the hub equations reduce, among others, to b-a+f=0, d-c-ωf=0, and -d-ω²g=0; the other three are a+e=0, g-b=0, and c-e=0. The supplied coefficients solve all six, with only f dropping out at ω=-1. The zero-flux square solves its four equations. Tail checkerboard parity gives the other energy, preserving every occupied site, and the energy difference is 2t in the stated time convention. No rational-flux assumption enters. I inspected the frozen nested verification/lieb5_flux_checker.py, which constructs the open matrix and checks numerical null vectors at five fluxes and both signs, plus finite candidate-edge enumeration. It was not run and does not certify infinite-lattice minimality or the printed symbolic witness; those follow from the analytic checks.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Knowing the minimum of ker B and that one can lift its elements supplies upper bounds only. The required opposite direction is an operator statement: every compact eigenstate at the specified nonzero energy must belong to the dimer-mode image. Without it a smaller Hubbard-vertex or mixed-support state is not excluded by the zero-mode result. This new reduction works uniformly in flux and proves physical support doubling as an exact relation. The proof of the 4/6/7 invariant itself is fully credited to the available equivalent machinery.

originality.rationale: The distinct supported claim is the all-flux exact physical-site minimum at the two nonzero energies of the twice-subdivided Hamiltonian, using the reduction that excludes original-vertex amplitudes and identifies the full compact eigenspaces at those energies. The 4/6/7 ground-graph circuit answer, the zero-flux eight-site mode, and two-band beating at zero flux are not novel. The strongest indexed result has exactly the same reduced incidence kernel but is a one-midpoint Hamiltonian at zero eigenvalue; it supplies the complete incidence minimum once the additional nonzero-energy dimer reduction is proved, not the target physical minimum or that reduction by itself.
residual_risks: A more general magnetic subdivision/eigenspace theorem or other physical application of gain-graph theory could explicitly subsume the dimer reduction; no such exact physical implication was established in the checked material.

value.rationale: The physically occupied-site cutoff matters for how many sites a localized input must address at either of the two flat-band energies of a single standard decorated lattice. The result proves sharp impossibility as well as constructions, including irrational flux: an arbitrarily small nonzero flux removes eight-site confinement, whereas the half-flux case allows twelve sites instead of the generic fourteen. Exact support transfer to both energy sectors also preserves the possibility of two-band beating within the same support. The value lies in the physical eigenspace and resource threshold, not in recounting the already covered incidence circuits.
